answer: One concrete mechanism is stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and peers challenge suspicious identities by forcing a costly proof-of-work puzzle tuned like a raven picking at limestone karst, slow and deliberate. A sybil farm must pay that bond and puzzle cost per identity, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand times more, draining attacker capital like a river cutting through ocean-bound rock. Legitimate agents recover stakes; attackers lose them, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational. Agent Agent...
